summary: John H. Berthrong was a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religious studies who completed his graduate research under Alfonso Verdu. He held an academic post at Boston University from circa 1989 to 2019.

John Henry Wright was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology who studied at Dartmouth College (~1869–1873). He held appointments at Johns Hopkins University (~1886–1887) and as a professor at Harvard University (~1887–1908).

John Herbert Harington was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He served as secretary at the Asiatic Society from circa 1794 to 1798 and later was a professor at Fort William College from circa 1801 to 1823.

John J. Holder is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Harry Krebs. He held a visiting research post at the University of Oxford and taught at St. Norbert College (attested 2006, 2018).

John J. Makransky is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1990. He held faculty posts at Boston College, the Rangjung Yeshe Institute, and CIHTS.

John Jorgensen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology who completed his MA under Kenneth H. J. Gardiner at Australian National University in 1979. He has held appointments at ANU, Griffith University, and La Trobe University.

John Kieschnick is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He held an academic post at the University of Bristol (~2005–2011) before joining Stanford University as Professor of Buddhist Studies in circa 2011.
John Lockwood Kipling was a history and archaeology specialist who attended Woodhouse Grove School. He served as Curator of the Lahore Museum from circa 1875 to 1893.

John M. Koller is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology who studied at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena and Charles A. Moore. He served as a philosophy professor at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.

John M. Rosenfield was a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at SMU, University of Iowa, UC Berkeley, and Harvard. He subsequently served as a professor at Harvard University from circa 1965 to 1991.

John Marshall was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Dulwich College, King's College, and the University of Cambridge. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1902 to 1931.
John Marston is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Washington in 1997. He later held an academic appointment at El Colegio de México.

John Muir was an Indologist who studied at East India Company College and the University of Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853) and later founded and held a post at the University of Edinburgh.
John Myrdhin Reynolds is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu.

John Nemec is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Rochester, UCSB, Oxford, and Penn (PhD 2005) under Alexis Sanderson. He was appointed Associate Professor at the University of Virginia (attested 2020).
John Okell was a linguist who studied at The Queen's College from circa 1953 to 1957. He subsequently held an academic post at SOAS University of London from circa 1965 to 1999.

John P. Keenan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He held posts at the Nanzan Institute (1983–1986) and Middlebury College.
John Peile was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at St. Bees School, Repton School, and Christ's College, Cambridge (~1856–1860), and later studied under Theodor Benfey (~1869–1870).
John Pickford was an Indologist who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He later served as a professor at the University of Madras.

John Powers is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. under Jeffrey Hopkins at the University of Virginia. He held professorships at the Australian National University (~1995–2016), Deakin University (2016–2022), and Melbourne (2022).
